sources.title: BlockFusion wins approval to reopen bitcoin mine on Frontier Avenue

profile.campus_note: One of 11 buildings OpenStreetMap contributors have mapped under this name in this locality, numbered west to east.
profile.research_note: Session 2026-09-03: local press names the operating entity "Northeast Data LLC" doing business as BlockFusion. All 10 OSM nodes for this name sit within ~250m of each other on the same Frontier Avenue industrial site and resolve to the same address via Nominatim reverse geocode; treated as one multi-building campus, not 10 distinct facilities.

reading.body:
BlockFusion Niagara Falls is a multi-building campus on Frontier Avenue in western New York that was reapproved in 2026 to operate in an industrial zone. The facility's published power capacity is not stated in the available operator specifications. No certifications qualifying the campus for particular workloads are published.

The campus ranks second among the one facility in New York with published power capacity, though this ranking reflects only the single megawatt figure disclosed by one other operator in the state. Of 31 mapped data center facilities across New York, only two have published power specifications, making this campus part of a sparse public record of capacity in the state. The Niagara Falls location sits near existing hydroelectric generation on the Niagara River, a factor relevant to power availability, though grid connection details are not published.

Without published power specifications, IT density, or intended use, the campus cannot be assessed against the compute constraints binding AI scaling. The operator's 2026 reapproval for bitcoin mining suggests the site's primary purpose at that date, but no specifications indicate whether the facility is configured, powered, or contracted for AI workloads.
